title: Why is there no network coverage in my area?
content:
Question: Why is there no network coverage in my area?

Answer: ### Short Answer

Coverage gaps can result from terrain/building obstruction, an outage under investigation, or the area being outside current tower footprint. Check Network > Coverage Map in the app for real-time status, or report the location so our Network team can log it for planning.

### Detailed Explanation

The three listed causes are meaningfully different in what a customer can do about them: obstruction is often a fixed physical constraint, an active outage is temporary and being worked on, and being outside the tower footprint is a coverage-planning issue — the coverage map and location-reporting flow exist to help distinguish which of the three applies.

### Key Details

| Detail | Value |
|---|---|
| Where to check | Network > Coverage Map in the app |
| Possible causes | Terrain/building obstruction; outage under investigation; outside current tower footprint |
| If none apply / for planning | Report the location for the Network team to log |

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Possible Cause | Diagnostic Check | Recommended Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| No coverage, area shown covered on map | Terrain/building obstruction, or a temporary outage | Coverage map status vs. Service Status for that area | Check both; if map shows covered but Service Status flags an outage, wait for restoration |
| No coverage, area shown outside footprint | Location is outside current tower coverage | Coverage map boundary for the exact location | Report the location so it can be logged for network planning |

### Escalation

Reporting the location to the Network team is the documented path when coverage is genuinely absent rather than temporarily degraded.

### Example Scenario

**Customer situation:** A customer has no signal at home and checks the app's coverage map.

**What happens:** If the map shows their area as covered, the likely cause is either obstruction or an active outage, best confirmed by checking Service Status; if the map shows the area outside the footprint, reporting the location is the relevant next step instead.
